description: Agent core in agent.py: LangGraph state + graph, the two tools (get_current_time, create_order), ChatBedrockConverse LLM bound to tools, authorization gate, human-in-the-loop interrupt before create_order, and the shared run_agent(conversation_id, user_text, whatsapp_number='') entry point wired to the DynamoDBSaver from FEAT-001. Depends on FEAT-001 (data.py, checkpointer.py). This is the shared core both triggers call.
steps: In agent.py define the graph state (TypedDict) with messages: Annotated[list, add_messages], authorized: bool, user_id: Optional[str], conversation_id: str, whatsapp_number: str.

Define tool get_current_time() returning a string with UTC ISO 8601 and a human-readable time. Define tool create_order(user_name, user_email, user_address, products, number_of_products, conversation_id) that HTTP POSTs to os.environ['ORDER_API_ENDPOINT'] a JSON body containing all six fields INCLUDING conversation_id, adds Authorization: Bearer {ORDER_API_KEY} when that env var is set, uses requests with a timeout, parses workflow_id from the response, and on success calls data.put_mapping(conversation_id, workflow_id, user_id, whatsapp_number) then returns a dict including workflow_id and a user-facing confirmation. user_id and whatsapp_number must come from graph state/config (e.g. injected via RunnableConfig or a closure), NOT from LLM-supplied tool args.

Build the LLM with langchain_aws.ChatBedrockConverse(model=os.environ.get('BEDROCK_MODEL_ID', <sensible Claude inference-profile default>)) and bind the two tools. Write a system prompt that: greets with a welcome, asks for the user ID to authorize, after authorization collects user_name, user_email, user_address, products, number_of_products, and asks for confirmation before ordering.

Assemble the StateGraph: an 'agent' node calling the tool-bound LLM; an authorization gate that, when not yet authorized, checks the typed id with data.is_authorized_user and either sets authorized/user_id or politely refuses and re-asks; a confirm step that calls langgraph.types.interrupt({...collected params...}) BEFORE create_order executes and only proceeds on an explicit affirmative resume value; a ToolNode (or equivalent) for the two tools; conditional edges routing model tool-calls -> confirm/interrupt -> tools -> back to agent. Compile with checkpointer=DynamoDBSaver().

Implement run_agent(conversation_id, user_text, whatsapp_number='')->str: config={'configurable': {'thread_id': conversation_id}}; detect a pending interrupt for the thread (via compiled_graph.get_state(config) / checkpointer.get_tuple) and, if paused, call graph.invoke(Command(resume=user_text), config); otherwise graph.invoke({'messages':[HumanMessage(user_text)], 'conversation_id':conversation_id, 'whatsapp_number':whatsapp_number, 'authorized':False, 'user_id':None}, config). Return the latest AI/interrupt text to show the user. Build the graph once at module scope for warm-reuse.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_agent.py covers and passes (Bedrock LLM, requests.post, and data.* mocked): (1) unauthorized id -> reply refuses and re-asks, no order; (2) authorized id -> proceeds to collect params; (3) all params collected -> interrupt fires and NO HTTP POST to ORDER_API_ENDPOINT occurs yet; (4) resume with 'yes' -> requests.post IS called with a body containing conversation_id and put_mapping is called with (conversation_id, workflow_id, user_id, whatsapp_number); (5) resume with 'no'/decline -> no POST.
create_order's POST body includes conversation_id and only includes ORDER_API_KEY Authorization header when the env var is set.
run_agent resumes a paused thread via Command(resume=...) rather than starting a new turn.
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_agent.py -q  (offline; Bedrock/requests/DynamoDB mocked; the five scenarios pass)
findings:
Implemented and verified offline. 6 new tests in tests/test_agent.py pass (the five FEAT-002 scenarios + an ORDER_API_KEY header check); full suite is 15 green. `python -c "import agent; assert hasattr(agent,'run_agent')"` passes.

PUBLIC SURFACE (for dependent features / app.py):
- run_agent(conversation_id, user_text, whatsapp_number='') -> str. Returns the text to show the user: the active interrupt's 'message' when paused, else the latest AIMessage text (handles str or list-of-blocks content). On a fresh thread it starts a new turn; on a paused thread it resumes. whatsapp_number defaults to '' (positional/kw). conversation_id is used as the checkpointer thread_id.
- agent.compiled_graph: the module-scope compiled StateGraph (built once at import with DynamoDBSaver()). build_graph(checkpointer=None) builds/compiles; passing a checkpointer (e.g. InMemorySaver) is how tests swap storage. agent._build_llm() returns ChatBedrockConverse(model=BEDROCK_MODEL_ID or default 'us.anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0', region=AWS_REGION).bind_tools(TOOLS); tests patch agent._build_llm to inject a fake LLM.
- Tools: get_current_time (@tool, no args) and create_order (@tool). TOOLS / TOOLS_BY_NAME exported. The create_order @tool is only the LLM-facing schema; the real work is place_order(**kwargs) which the tools node calls.

HOW user_id / whatsapp_number REACH create_order (NOT from the LLM):
- AgentState (TypedDict) carries: messages (add_messages), authorized: bool, user_id: Optional[str], conversation_id: str, whatsapp_number: str.
- The custom tools_node reads the last AIMessage's tool_calls. For 'create_order' it discards the model-supplied conversation_id/identity and calls place_order(..., conversation_id=state['conversation_id'], user_id=state.get('user_id'), whatsapp_number=state.get('whatsapp_number','')). place_order POSTs JSON {user_name,user_email,user_address,products,number_of_products,conversation_id} to os.environ['ORDER_API_ENDPOINT'] with timeout=30, adds 'Authorization: Bearer {ORDER_API_KEY}' only when that env var is set, raise_for_status, parses response.json()['workflow_id'], then data.put_mapping(conversation_id, workflow_id, user_id, whatsapp_number) and returns {'workflow_id', 'message'}.
- Authorization: authorize_node is the entry node (START->authorize). It reads the last HumanMessage text; if data.is_authorized_user(text) it sets authorized=True, user_id=text; otherwise it appends a polite re-ask AIMessage and routes to END (no LLM, no order). Only when authorized does it route to the 'agent' node.

INTERRUPT / RESUME DETECTION APPROACH:
- Graph edges: authorize -(authorized?)-> agent|END; agent -(route_after_agent)-> END (no tool_calls) | 'confirm' (any create_order tool_call) | 'tools' (other tools); confirm -(route_after_confirm)-> 'tools'|END; tools -> agent.
- confirm_node calls langgraph.types.interrupt({'type':'confirm_order','message':...,'parameters':<collected args>}) BEFORE create_order runs. The resume value is read back from interrupt(); _is_affirmative() accepts True or yes/y/confirm/ok/sure/proceed etc. Non-affirmative appends a cancel ToolMessage + AIMessage and routes to END (no POST).
- run_agent detects a paused thread via compiled_graph.get_state(config).next being non-empty; if paused it invokes Command(resume=user_text); otherwise it invokes the initial state dict. The user-facing interrupt text is pulled from get_state(config).interrupts[-1].value['message'].

TEST APPROACH (fully offline, no AWS/network): patch agent._build_llm -> FakeLLM scripting AIMessage(s); patch agent.data.is_authorized_user and agent.data.put_mapping (MagicMock); patch agent.requests.post (MagicMock returning .json()->{'workflow_id':'wf-777'}); rebuild graph with InMemorySaver and monkeypatch agent.compiled_graph. ORDER_API_ENDPOINT set via env, ORDER_API_KEY deleted/set per test.

NOTES: Built against installed langgraph 1.1.3 / langgraph-checkpoint 4.0.0 / langchain-aws 1.4.1 / langchain-core 1.6.3 (matches FEAT-001's recorded deviation from context.json pins). Did NOT edit handler.py or whatsapp_lambda.py. requirements.txt still unreconciled (left for a later step per FEAT-001 findings).
